subject: general
question: What is net investment?

options.text: Sum of all the investments in a country

solution:
The correct answer is __**Gross investment - depreciation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A company's net investment is the sum of its expenditures on capital assets less the cost of depreciating those assets.
 
• This gives an idea of the actual spending on durable products utilized by the company in its operations, such as buildings, machinery, and software.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Depreciation: It means a fall in the value of an asset because of usage or with efflux of time or due to obsolescence or accident.
 
• Appreciation: It means an increase in the value of an asset over time. This the opposite of depreciation. It is an upward adjustment of the value of an asset held on a company's accounting book.
 
• Deceleration: It is the rate at which an asset's value in the market goes down.
 
• Gross investment: It is the total amount spent on goods in order to produce other goods and services. 
 
• Net investment: It is the amount of increase in productive stock.
 
• 
 
Capital investment is the money used by a business to purchase fixed assets, such as land, machinery, or buildings. The money may be in the form of cash, assets, or loans. Without capital investment, businesses may have a hard time getting off the ground.
